key_insight: HiVe-Mem proposes interleaving broader memory retrieval with query-specific evidence assembly, helping multimodal agents find relevant past information and use it more effectively.
problem_solved: Semantic search over compressed memories can miss relevant interactions, while fixed memory representations may not provide the different kinds of evidence each query needs.
method: Horizontal memory expansion: broaden the search for relevant information across an agent’s interaction history.
Vertical evidence composition: assemble evidence suited to the current query rather than relying only on predefined memory representations.
Interleave these two processes within a multimodal memory framework.
impact: This approach could improve how long-running multimodal agents use past interactions to answer new questions. The provided abstract is truncated, so implementation details and performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Interaction-history timeline showing text, image, and other multimodal memories.
Horizontal branching diagram illustrating expansion toward additional relevant memories.
Vertical evidence stack showing multiple pieces of information assembled for one query.
Alternating-arrow loop connecting memory expansion and evidence composition.
paper_title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
paper_authors: Haozhen Zhang, Bohan Liu, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Haodong Yue
